questions.question: What is the Next.js 16 file/function name for what used to be `middleware.ts` / `export function middleware`?
questions.explanation: Next.js 16 renamed the convention to proxy.ts with an exported proxy function; having both proxy.ts and middleware.ts in the same project is an error.

questions.question: What does the `config.matcher` option control?
options: Which database the app connects to
Which request paths run through the proxy function
The order routes are rendered in
questions.explanation: Without a matcher, the proxy function runs on every request, including static assets; matcher patterns scope it to only the routes that need it.

questions.question: Why does redirecting unauthenticated users in the proxy function (rather than inside the page component) matter?
options: It runs before the route starts rendering, avoiding wasted Server Component work for unauthorized requests
It's the only place NextResponse.redirect is available
It automatically caches the redirect forever
questions.explanation: The proxy runs ahead of routing, so an unauthorized request is redirected before any page/data-fetching code executes.

questions.question: Which statement about the proxy runtime in Next.js 16 is correct?
options: It runs only in the Edge runtime, without filesystem access
It runs on the Node.js runtime, and setting the runtime option in proxy.ts throws an error
It runs only for GET requests
questions.explanation: Since Next.js 16, proxy defaults to the Node.js runtime and the runtime segment option is not allowed in proxy files. Because it runs on every matched request, it should still stay lightweight.
